Explain why sodium ions cross cell surface membranes by these mechanisms and not by
simple diffusion.

Explain the mode of action of an enzyme that uses the induced fit mechanism.

State what is meant by the term extracellular.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Name the bacterium that causes cholera.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Describe how cholera is transmitted from an infected person to an uninfected person.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Suggest and explain why cholera outbreaks are common after natural disasters.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The bacteria that cause cholera can become resistant to antibiotics by a substitution mutation.
A substitution mutation occurs when one nucleotide in the DNA sequence is replaced by a
different nucleotide.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Explain how a substitution mutation could result in a change in the amino acid sequence
of a polypeptide.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The antibiotic nalidixic acid acts as an inhibitor of an enzyme involved in DNA replication
in the bacteria that cause cholera.
The gene gyrA codes for this enzyme. A substitution mutation in this gene results in
resistance to the antibiotic nalidixic acid.
Suggest how a change in the amino acid sequence of the enzyme results in antibiotic
resistance.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Some of the strains of bacteria that cause cholera are resistant to more than one antibiotic
(multiple resistance).
Discuss the consequences of multiple resistance for health authorities.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) have been used in the treatment of some non-infectious
diseases.
MAbs can be designed to bind to a protein on diseased cells, so causing their destruction by
cells of the person’s immune system.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Name the part of an antibody molecule that will bind to a protein on diseased cells.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest how the binding of monoclonal antibody to the diseased cells causes their
destruction by cells of the person’s immune system.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Myasthenia gravis is an auto-immune disease.
Explain the term auto-immune disease.

Smoking causes changes to the structure of the lining of the bronchi that make smokers more
likely to be infected by bacteria.
Describe these changes and explain how this leads to an increased risk of bacterial infection.

Describe what causes oxygen to be released from the oxyhaemoglobin as blood flows through
respiring tissues.
